name: Lisbon
tagline: The secret pastel de nata recipe from 1837, and 26 kitchens under the roof of an 1892 market.

Pastéis de Belém.description: The original pastel de nata factory, with a secret recipe since 1837.

Sol e Pesca.description: A former fishing-tackle shop turned tinned-fish bar in Cais do Sodré. Anthony Bourdain visited on "No Reservations."

Belcanto.description: Chef José Avillez's flagship table in Chiado, Lisbon's most awarded restaurant. Two Michelin stars.

Cervejaria Ramiro.description: Lisbon's benchmark seafood house since the 1950s, with shrimp, barnacles, and cold beer, just like always.

A Ginjinha Sem Rival.description: A historic ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) bar with more than a century of history, next to Praça dos Restauradores.

A Ginjinha.description: The original ginjinha kiosk by Largo de São Domingos, pouring sour-cherry liqueur since 1840. Anthony Bourdain stopped here on "No Reservations."

Cantinho do Avillez.description: Chef José Avillez's casual Chiado tavern, with reinvented classics like tempura green beans and pork cheek. Anthony Bourdain dined here with the chef himself on "No Reservations."

100 Maneiras.description: Bosnian chef Ljubomir Stanisic's fine-dining spot in Bairro Alto, built around a surprise tasting menu. Anthony Bourdain visited on "No Reservations"; it held a Michelin star until losing it in 2026.

Alma.description: Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's two-Michelin-star table in Chiado, set inside a former codfish warehouse. Anthony Bourdain dined here on "No Reservations."

O Trevo.description: A small kiosk-bar on Praça Luís de Camões, known for its bifana (marinated pork sandwich). Anthony Bourdain tried one on "No Reservations."

Cura.description: The Four Seasons Ritz Lisbon's one-Michelin-star restaurant, rooted in Portuguese tradition and currently led by chef Rodolfo Lavrador.

Loco.description: A 22-seat restaurant in Santos from chef Alexandre Silva, built around a surprise tasting menu rooted in Portuguese tradition. One Michelin star.

Feitoria.description: The Altis Belém Hotel's riverside restaurant, holding a Michelin star since 2011 under chef André Cruz.

Epur.description: French chef Vincent Farges' Chiado restaurant, with Tagus views across three dining rooms and a Michelin star since 2019.

Eleven.description: A panoramic restaurant by Eduardo VII Park, led by German chef Joachim Koerper since 2004; a fixture of Lisbon fine dining for two decades.

A Cevicheria.description: Chef Kiko Martins' ceviche bar in Príncipe Real, with a giant wooden octopus hanging over the counter and a line out the door most nights.

Zunzum Gastrobar.description: Chef Marlene Vieira's gastrobar by Doca Jardim do Tabaco, known for seafood rice and codfish à brás; awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2024.

Solar dos Presuntos.description: A 40-plus-year classic near Restauradores specializing in Minho-region cooking: lamprey, fried shad, and seafood rice.

Taberna da Rua das Flores.description: Chef André Magalhães' tiny no-reservations tavern in Chiado, with a chalkboard menu that changes daily with the market.

Cervejaria Trindade.description: Lisbon's oldest beer hall, opened in 1836 inside a former convent, famed for its 19th-century tile panels.

Clube de Fado.description: A fado house in Alfama next to the Cathedral, serving Portuguese dinner with nightly performances by acclaimed fadistas in a 17th-century building.

Solar do Vinho do Porto.description: A tasting bar run by the Port and Douro Wine Institute, open since 1946 in Bairro Alto, with hundreds of Port wines on the list.

Tasca do Chico.description: A fado vadio tavern in Bairro Alto where professionals and regulars alike take turns singing; Anthony Bourdain sat here with writer António Lobo Antunes.

Manteigaria.description: An open-kitchen pastel de nata factory in Chiado, widely considered Belém's best rival thanks to its butter-laden pastry.

Café Martinho da Arcada.description: Lisbon's oldest café, open since 1782 under the arcades of Praça do Comércio and a favorite haunt of Fernando Pessoa, who wrote part of his work here.

A Brasileira.description: A historic 1905 café in Chiado, with a bronze statue of Fernando Pessoa seated on its terrace; a meeting point for writers and intellectuals.

Confeitaria Nacional.description: Lisbon's oldest confectionery, founded in 1829 on Praça da Figueira, famed for its bolo-rei and traditional pastries.

Pastelaria Versailles.description: An Art Nouveau tea room from 1922 in Avenidas Novas, with mirrors, chandeliers, and old-fashioned table service.

Time Out Market Lisboa.description: Time Out's food hall inside the historic 1892 Mercado da Ribeira, with 26 restaurants and 8 bars under one roof.

Mercado de Campo de Ourique.description: A 1934 neighborhood market reborn as a local food hall, with stalls for sushi, pizza, burgers, and wine.

Canalha.description: Chef João Rodrigues' restaurant on the edge of Belém, with produce on display and a daily lunch special on the chalkboard; awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Prado.description: Chef António Galapito's farm-to-table restaurant near the Cathedral, built around organic, seasonal ingredients in an industrial-style space.

Boi-Cavalo.description: A small restaurant in Alfama set inside a former butcher's shop, serving reinvented Lisbon cooking at a good price.

Sea Me.description: A modern fishmonger-restaurant in Chiado that combines a fish counter, sushi bar, and grill for fresh catch picked out on the spot.

Pastelaria Aloma.description: A Campo de Ourique pastry shop open since 1943, repeatedly named (most recently in 2024) Lisbon's best pastel de nata in the national contest.

Casa do Alentejo.description: A 17th-century palace turned Alentejo regional clubhouse in 1932, with a Moorish courtyard and a dining room serving Alentejo cooking at down-to-earth prices.

Pizzaria Luzzo.description: A Neapolitan-style pizzeria with several locations in Lisbon, prized for its long-fermented dough and wood-fired oven.

Café Nicola.description: A century-old Art Deco café on Rossio square, historically tied to the poet Bocage, whose statue stands in the square outside.

Pinóquio.description: A classic seafood house on Praça dos Restauradores, with a terrace and platters of shellfish and garlic shrimp served for decades.

Chapitô à Mesa.description: A restaurant perched above the Chapitô circus school in Alfama, with a panoramic terrace over Lisbon's rooftops and the Tagus.
